column1: # Feature-level evidence co-anchors (P4 cross-anchor record; W23-B).
# One row per extra hand-declared nextest test id that proves a named clause of
# an already-anchored `(feature_id, frontend)` cell in `feature_evidence.tsv`.
# That cell's primary `test_id` keeps its meaning and stays the single anchor
# authority: this table only records further discoverable evidence for a clause
# whose production surface the primary anchor test does not drive.  It cannot
# make a cell `Ready` (the Rust G2 closure reads `feature_evidence.tsv` alone)
# and it never replaces the primary anchor.
# Why a side table instead of a sixth column: the Rust consumer
# (`crates/taskmanager-ui-contract/src/feature_coverage/platform_gate/evidence.rs`)
# embeds `feature_evidence.tsv` with `include_str!` and accepts exactly the
# five committed columns, so a sixth column is a hard schema cutover that must
# change `crates/**` in the same commit.  Until that window, the optional
# column is materialized sparsely here, keyed by the cell it extends; the
# resolver reads both tables in one pass (`--co-anchors`, default on, fail
# closed when the file is missing).
# Columns (TAB separated):
#   feature_id   stable `FeatureId` id naming an anchored row of
#                `feature_evidence.tsv` for the same frontend
#   frontend     gpui | iced | tui | bevy
#   co_test_id   the extra nextest test path, exactly as `cargo nextest list`
#                reports it for the owning frontend
#   reason       the definition clause this co-anchor proves (never `-`)
# Discipline: exactly like every other anchor -- declared by hand, resolved by
# set membership against discovery, never derived by scanning Rust source; a
# renamed or deleted co-anchor is `dangling` and fails the run, and a row that
# names a cell without an anchored feature-evidence row (or repeats that cell's
# primary anchor) is `invalid`.
feature_id
